q: The Popov criterion for absolute stability of a feedback system with a sector nonlinearity φ (0 ≤ φ(y)/y ≤ K) requires the existence of a constant q ≥ 0 such that:
opts: The Nyquist plot of G lies to the right of −1/K
exp: Popov's criterion (1961): absolute stability holds if (1+iqω)G(iω) + 1/K has nonnegative real part for some q ≥ 0. The Popov line in the Nyquist diagram separates stable from unstable. Stronger than the circle criterion, Popov's condition is less conservative.
